scope: Application/API isolation using authenticated owner identity, PostgreSQL schemas, owner-derived encryption and private media paths.
passed_boundaries: Twenty simultaneous logins enqueue separate owner sync requests
Separate Page and System User stores even with matching connection and Page IDs
A second owner's encryption key cannot decrypt the first owner's token
Identical uploaded bytes deduplicate within one owner and retain twenty distinct owner assets
The same request UUID resolves to a different private schedule in each of twenty owners
Canceling one owner's schedule preserves the other nineteen schedules
The same video ID has distinct owner metrics, history and events
Forged internal/workspace headers and user query parameters cannot change gateway owner identity
Admin and owner MCP tokens both resolve business data in their own namespace
MCP arguments cannot select another workspace
Disabling one owner invalidates their sessions and MCP tokens while another owner remains usable

frontend_fix.before: Responses and upload results from an older session were accepted after an account transition; a delayed 401 could expire the newer session. Auth changes were not synchronized to other tabs.
frontend_fix.after: Changed sessions discard stale responses and uploads. Login/logout/expiry clears other tabs' cached views and composers through a credential-free storage notification.

verification.local_worker_engine: Disposable in-memory PGlite development socket; native concurrency is verified separately in CI

limits: This verifies application users; database/OS operators still have infrastructure access and account administrators retain password reset powers.
One browser profile shares a session cookie across tabs; simultaneous independent accounts use separate profiles.
The audit is not a sustained load benchmark or proof of twenty simultaneous Meta publications.
